title: Aragon-legacy governance — ACL permission-manager escalation (grantPermission -> transfer)
closed_reasons: vote creation is gated: CREATE_VOTES_ROLE is held by the DAO's TokenManager (holder-gated forward) or an EOA, not ANY, in the overwhelming majority of DAOs
governance tokens are illiquid: no funded DAO token has an AMM pool deep enough to buy minAQ*totalSupply; the top minAQ=0 candidates have no pool at all (DexScreener: no pairs)
voting power uses a block-1 snapshot (balanceOfAt(block.number-1)) so the quorum is not flash-loanable in one transaction
the 46 DAOs whose governance token totalSupply==0 (incl. the 100-ETH DAP) are permanently stuck (S)
key_facts: The Voting app IS the ACL permission-manager for the holding app's TRANSFER_ROLE on 2,002 of 2,202 funded DAOs (227.3013 ETH); an executed proposal can grantPermission(voting, holding, TRANSFER_ROLE) then holding.transfer(...) - fork-proven (2 ETH moved from Agent 0xbcd768c5)
Independent sample re-read: 107/116 (92.2%) manager - consistent with 2,002/2,202 (90.9%)
TokenManager.forward(bytes) lets any token holder create a vote (TokenManager holds CREATE_VOTES_ROLE on 1,941/2,002 funded DAOs); ANY-open newVote exists on a minority
E-U-conditional exposure = 227.3013 ETH (~$534,466 at $2,351.36/ETH); of this 100.104 ETH (~$235,380) is stuck (S, 46 DAOs) and 127.197 ETH (~$299,086) is governance-movable (P)

Closest cases: DAO 0xf6b32eee (1.71 ETH, token BBIZ supply=2, minAQ=0, TokenManager) needs only 1 token; 0xa323b631 (0.30 ETH, minAQ=0); the ANT DAO 0x2de83b50 (2.20 ETH, liquid ANT, minAQ=0) is creation-gated (no TokenManager, CREATE_VOTES_ROLE on EOA 0xcafE1A77)
Largest funded with an existing but empty pool: 0x001cd74c (14.024 ETH, token SHILL, minAQ=30%); its Uni V2 WETH pool holds 0.0856 SHILL of the 75,674 needed

Prior verdict reconciliation: our $0 number was correct, but our mechanism/trigger was wrong - we tested direct holding.transfer (APP_AUTH_FAILED, the pre-escalation state) and relied on '0 voteTime=0', which is true but non-decisive; the real trigger is a token AMM listing
caveats: The PoC's end-to-end tests simulate token acquisition by minting the governance token from its controller; they prove the mechanism, not that the tokens are acquirable today
The attack spans multiple blocks and voteTime (6-48h); it is buyable-if-listed, not atomic
46 custom-appId Aragon apps (Lido/API3) are outside the standard-voting census; none is a funded holding app with the escalation relationship
Point-in-time reads 2026-10-25; re-read all state before acting
DexScreener cross-check is rate-limited; the exhaustive pool scan uses Uniswap V2/V3 + Sushi factories only
one_liner: External unprivileged attacker can extract ~$0 live from Aragon-legacy DAOs today; the ACL escalation (Voting grants itself the holding app's TRANSFER_ROLE, then transfers) is real and fork-proven on 2,002/2,202 funded DAOs (227.3 ETH ~ $534k), but is gated by token illiquidity + vote-creation + a 1-block snapshot - it re-arms the moment any affected DAO token gets an AMM listing. Our prior $0 was right but for the wrong reason.
